claims.content: Allow users to compress one or more objects into one or more compressed archive volumes using supported formats.

goal.raw_text: Allow users to compress one or more objects into one or more compressed archive volumes using supported formats.

claims.content: User
The PeaZip application is running and the user has access to the file manager interface.
One or more objects (files or archives) exist in the computer system that are available for selection.
The user has not yet initiated the archive creation process via any of the defined stimulus sequences.

The user initiates the archive creation process by selecting one or more objects and choosing an action such as 'Create archive' from the File menu, 'Go to archiving layout' from the Browser submenu, pressing the 'Add' button on the toolbar, or using the context menu options 'Add' or 'Add to separate archives'.

trigger.raw_text: The user initiates the archive creation process by selecting one or more objects and choosing an action such as 'Create archive' from the File menu, 'Go to archiving layout' from the Browser submenu, pressing the 'Add' button on the toolbar, or using the context menu options 'Add' or 'Add to separate archives'.

claims.content: The user selects the compression format from a list of supported formats.
The user chooses the storage space (location) where the archive is going to be saved.
The user sets the archive's name.
The user defines what should happen in case of existence of a homonym file or archive in the selected storage space.
The user optionally splits the selected objects' data content into more than one archive volume.
The user optionally appends a timestamp to the created archive's name for archiving and backup purposes.
The user optionally sets a password and keyfile to encrypt ('lock') the created archives.
The system creates the compressed archive, potentially joining multiple objects' content into a single unit.
If the user selects an unsupported compression format, the system does not allow proceeding with archive creation.
The user may choose to run PeaZip as a different user, which closes the current instance and opens a new one under an alternative user profile.
The user may quickly change the application’s language via the 'Localization' option, selecting from a list of supported languages.
The user may access the Settings Interface to configure parameters such as default archive format, character encoding, GUI appearance, toolbar buttons, and backend command-line applications.
The user may define the path for the location of the computer system that is going to be considered by PeaZip as its Desktop.
The user may set policy about PeaLauncher window’s behavior after some function’s termination.
The user may have choices on recently managed archives history utility.
The user may choose a selection of users’ favorite archiving and compression formats to be offered for quick selection and which format should be used as default in create archive interface.
The user may configure parameters of the features of archive creation and archive content extraction.
The user may choose applications for opening/previewing contents of managed by PeaZip archives.
The user may configure parameters of computer system’s files and archives management tools.
The user may adapt the application’s graphical interface to their needs, modifying color, icons, fonts, window opacity and size for GUI, and toolbar buttons.
A compressed archive is created in the selected storage space with the user-specified name and format.
If enabled, a timestamp is appended to the created archive’s name for archiving and backup purposes.
If specified by the user, the archive is encrypted ('locked') using a password and/or keyfile.
If volume splitting was selected, the archive content is split into multiple volumes of user-defined size.
Multiple objects’ content are joined into a single compressed archive unit (unless split into volumes).
